scope: Five H1 qualification cases for the installed, pinned local Temporal toolchain. They verify toolchain behavior and an isolated synthetic workflow only; they do not implement the B03 business workflow/outbox or establish AT-05, AT-16, AT-29, AT-09, or production acceptance.

installed_toolchain.python: Pinned CPython 3.12 interpreter at toolchain-root/venv/bin/python; capture exact version and interpreter SHA-256 at execution.
installed_toolchain.temporalio: 1.34.0 in the isolated 36-package environment; all 32 pre-existing package versions remain unchanged.
installed_toolchain.inspection_already_done: The installed binary was used only for --version and --help. No server was started. The observed start-dev options include --ip, --port, --http-port, --metrics-port, --db-filename, and --headless; global help exposes --disable-config-env, --disable-config-file, and --env-file.

case_inventory.purpose: Verify the approved installation matches the candidate package and binary pins.
case_inventory.target: Isolated Python environment, 36-package lock, explicit Temporal CLI binary.
case_inventory.method: Read package metadata from the pinned interpreter, independently compare the 32 original package versions and four added package records to the reviewed lock, invoke only the explicit CLI path with --version, and hash the executable.
case_inventory.agent: TC runs assertions; main owns the isolated installation and artifact manifest; independent reviewer audits the exact execution contract and evidence.
pass_criteria: Exactly 36 locked packages are installed, with all 32 original package versions unchanged and the four additions exactly matching the reviewed lock.
The explicit Python interpreter is CPython 3.12 and imports temporalio 1.34.0.
The explicit CLI reports 1.9.1 / Server 1.32.0 and its SHA-256 equals 712217694cac9f786a72d4b6c876cd15f3dcf1bf31434d9fed6af25242a327a0.
No global package state, repository lock, or source file changes during qualification.
case_inventory.expected_result: All exact versions and hashes match; any mismatch stops the remaining H1 cases before server startup.
case_inventory.evidence: Private interpreter/package inventory and artifact hashes; public summary contains only versions, counts, and digests.
case_inventory.recovery: Preserve the failed candidate and sanitized result; do not change versions or silently install a fallback. Resolve through same-SHA review.
case_inventory.scope_impact: Installation evidence does not by itself establish SDK/CLI runtime compatibility.

case_inventory.purpose: Prove the launch guard rejects a hash-mismatched executable before it runs.
case_inventory.target: Main-owned verified CLI launch guard and a harmless private sentinel executable.
case_inventory.method: Provide a syntactically valid but wrong expected hash for the sentinel; call the same launch guard used for actual server startup and assert the fixed hash-mismatch error and a zero sentinel invocation count.
case_inventory.agent: TC owns the sentinel and assertions; main owns the verifier/launcher; reviewer checks the guard precedes process creation.
pass_criteria: The launch guard returns the fixed hash mismatch classification.
The sentinel records zero executions and no server process or data directory is created.
No PATH fallback, alternate binary, or implicit download is attempted.
case_inventory.evidence: Private sentinel count, expected/actual digest summary, process inventory, and fixed error code without executable contents.
case_inventory.recovery: Preserve the negative fixture and failure record; correct only the approved artifact pin or launch guard after review.
case_inventory.scope_impact: A negative sentinel cannot replace the positive real CLI integration case.

case_inventory.purpose: Verify missing and truncated binaries are rejected before any process launch.
case_inventory.target: Main-owned CLI artifact verifier and launch guard.
case_inventory.method: Parameterize a nonexistent executable path and a truncated executable with a matching manifest digest. Assert the fixed invalid-artifact classification and zero process/sentinel starts in each case.
case_inventory.agent: TC provides independent temporary fixtures; main owns validation; reviewer checks no fallback behavior.
pass_criteria: Both parameters fail before process creation with their contract-pinned error code.
No server data directory, alternate artifact, or download is created or invoked.
case_inventory.expected_result: Both malformed or absent artifacts fail closed; the collected case count is exactly 2.
case_inventory.evidence: Per-parameter digest, fixed result code, process count, and isolated directory summary.
case_inventory.recovery: Retain both parameter outcomes; never retry against a default or globally installed executable.
case_inventory.scope_impact: These are verifier boundary cases, not CLI server behavior tests.

case_inventory.purpose: Prove actual local Temporal persistent history and pinned workflow identity survive a real CLI server restart, and running/closed IDs cannot be reused.
case_inventory.target: Actual CLI 1.9.1 process, private SQLite file, SDK 1.34.0 client/worker processes, and one deterministic synthetic signal-wait workflow.
method: Create a fresh mode-0700 private attempt directory and a private persistent SQLite database path. Start the explicit CLI with the observed supported options: --disable-config-env --disable-config-file --env-file <fresh private empty file>, then server start-dev --ip 127.0.0.1 --port <allocated> --http-port <allocated> --metrics-port <allocated> --db-filename <private path> --headless. Use distinct allocated loopback ports and the exact reviewed CLI argv; do not use ambient Temporal env/config files, WorkflowEnvironment, or SDK server-download helpers.

Readiness is bounded to 30 seconds and requires SDK Client.connect plus workflow_service.describe_namespace. Describe the namespace and assert its retention exceeds 3600 seconds before admitting the fixture workflow.

Start separate recorded client and worker processes using a literal task queue and workflow ID. The synthetic workflow records a fixed start marker, waits on one named signal, then returns a fixed literal result. Worker/query readiness is bounded to 15 seconds; RPC deadline is 5 seconds.

Wait up to 30 seconds for history to show the exact blocked signal-wait state. Capture workflow ID, run ID, and a normalized ordered history-event summary. While it is running, attempt a duplicate start using ID_REUSE_POLICY_REJECT_DUPLICATE and ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL; require the version-pinned typed already-started exception, same original run ID, and unchanged history.

Stop the exact worker and client processes, then the server, each with a 10-second graceful deadline followed only by a 5-second owned-process cleanup deadline. Assert each recorded PID/start-time handle is gone before restart. Restart the exact CLI binary against the same SQLite path and ports; create new client and worker processes rather than reusing old SDK connections.

After readiness, retrieve the exact workflow ID and assert the same run ID and unchanged pre-restart history prefix. Start the new worker, signal the existing workflow once, and assert the fixed result and exact appended history. Do not issue another workflow start after restart.

After completion, try to start the same workflow ID again with the same reject policies; require the typed duplicate/closed-execution error and assert one logical execution/run ID, unchanged completed result, and unchanged history. Stop and reap all exact process handles.
case_inventory.agent: TC owns the synthetic workflow, exact history/run-ID oracles and integration test; main owns explicit-binary verification and service/worker fixture lifecycle; independent reviewer approves exact SDK/CLI error classification and process protocol before execution.
pass_criteria: All server, client and worker processes use the reviewed explicit binaries/interpreter and remain local to allocated loopback endpoints.

CLI config environment and config file discovery are explicitly disabled; the only env file is the fresh empty private fixture, and ambient TEMPORAL_* settings cannot change ports, storage, namespace, or server mode.
Namespace DescribeNamespace readback confirms retention strictly greater than 3600 seconds.
The running duplicate and post-close duplicate are both rejected with the pinned typed SDK exception and cannot create a second run.
The workflow is blocked before shutdown, then resumes after restart with byte-equivalent normalized history prefix, the same workflow ID/run ID, one signal, and exactly one literal result.
The restart uses the identical private SQLite path and exact CLI binary, with no replacement in-memory store or new workflow start.
Every worker/client/server is terminated and its PID plus process start-time is verified absent; no unrelated process is signaled.
case_inventory.expected_result: Exactly one synthetic logical run remains with the same workflow ID and run ID across server restart, and its durable history is extended only by the signal and completion events.
case_inventory.evidence: Private argv/stdout/stderr, per-process PID/start-time lifecycle records, private store identity, namespace-retention value, typed duplicate error codes, and before/restart/after normalized history summaries. Public evidence contains hashes/counts only, not raw history or local paths.
case_inventory.recovery: The full integration attempt has a 240-second deadline inside the 300-second Python phase. On timeout, retain the SQLite file and all logs, poll/clean only the recorded process handles, and mark the attempt failed. Never erase/recreate history to retry or claim the old run resumed without matching IDs/history.
case_inventory.scope_impact: This is one synthetic Temporal primitive. It does not prove IFPMIC PostgreSQL durability, outbox redelivery, the 29-node business workflow, human acceptance, B03 H2-H5, or any original AT case.

execution_limits_and_safety.network: The actual Temporal server, client and worker communicate only over loopback on fresh, allocated ports. No remote Temporal, Paperclip database, company IdP, or public endpoint is used.
execution_limits_and_safety.storage: A new private versioned SQLite file is used for each integration attempt and reused only for that attempt's restart. It is Temporal server storage, never IFPMIC business PostgreSQL.
execution_limits_and_safety.process_ownership: Capture exact PID and process start-time for CLI, worker and client before waiting. On timeout, inspect the same handles; never use process-name matching or infer termination from a port closing.
execution_limits_and_safety.implicit_downloads_and_config: Forbidden. Start the actual verified CLI executable directly with --disable-config-env --disable-config-file and a fresh empty private --env-file plus explicit reviewed server arguments; no WorkflowEnvironment, SDK-managed server installation, ambient Temporal config/env discovery, default PATH fallback, or server download helper.
execution_limits_and_safety.source_and_privacy: Capture source/artifact hashes before execution, private stdout/stderr and lifecycle evidence with restrictive permissions, and public sanitized summaries only. No credentials, unredacted environment, raw history, or private filesystem path is published.

pending_execution_contract_decisions: Pin exact CLI 1.9.1 start-dev argv and whether the three separate loopback ports are all required by the reviewed deployment mode.
Pin exact Python SDK 1.34.0 DescribeNamespace request/response field and the typed exception class/code for running and closed duplicate starts.
Pin exact worker/client subprocess entrypoint and how the synthetic workflow module is made importable without adding unreviewed packages or retaining a process across restart.
Pin readiness polling cadence, retryable startup errors, graceful-stop signal, and exact owned-process kill/reap protocol within the listed deadlines.
Pin exact normalized history fields/events and storage-path identity check, excluding nondeterministic timestamps while retaining event order and workflow/run identity.

acceptance_boundary.H1: Not accepted until all five cases pass, exact toolchain/source pins match, process cleanup and private evidence are independently reviewed.
acceptance_boundary.H2_to_H7: Not authorized by this H1 test plan.
acceptance_boundary.original_AT_01_to_AT_32: not executed or accepted by H1 qualification
